# Earth — Digital Twin

A photo-realistic, interactive 3D digital twin of Earth running entirely in the browser (WebGL / Three.js, no build step).

## Run

Double-click `serve.cmd` (or run `python -m http.server 8090` in this folder) and open http://localhost:8090.

A local server is required because the app uses ES modules; opening `index.html` directly via `file://` will not work.

## Features

- **8K NASA Blue Marble imagery** with terrain normal mapping and ocean specular sun glint
- **Real sun position** — the day/night terminator is computed from the actual UTC time using a solar ephemeris (subsolar point shown in the HUD)
- **City lights** that fade in as the terminator sweeps past, with sunset-reddened light near the twilight zone
- **Animated cloud layer** that drifts relative to the surface
- **Atmospheric scattering shell** — blue rim glow shading into sunset orange at the terminator
- **Time machine** — pause, accelerate up to 1 day/sec, or run time backwards; `NOW` snaps back to real time
- **Location search** (OpenStreetMap Nominatim) with cinematic fly-to
- **Click anywhere** to drop a marker, reverse-geocode the place, and see its local solar time; double-click to fly in
- **Live ISS tracking** (wheretheiss.at API) with ground-track trail — enable in Layers
- **Layers panel** — toggle clouds, atmosphere, city lights, Milky Way, graticule, auto-rotate
- **HUD** — cursor lat/lon, camera altitude in km, subsolar point

Search, reverse geocoding, and ISS tracking need internet; everything else runs fully offline from local assets.

## Controls

| Action | Input |
|---|---|
| Orbit | drag |
| Zoom | scroll (speed adapts to altitude) |
| Inspect location | click |
| Fly to location | double-click or search |

## Credits

- Imagery: NASA Blue Marble / Visible Earth via [Solar System Scope textures](https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/) (CC-BY-4.0)
- Normal & specular maps: three.js examples
- Geocoding: © OpenStreetMap contributors (Nominatim)
- ISS telemetry: wheretheiss.at
